name: Os
description: Configuration of the Os (Operating System) module.

children.name: OsAlarm
children.description: An OsAlarm may be used to asynchronously inform or activate a specific task. It is possible to start alarms automatically at system start-up depending on the application mode.

children.name: OsAlarmAccessingApplication
children.description: Reference to applications which have an access to this object.

children.name: OsAlarmCounterRef
children.description: Reference to the assigned counter for that alarm

children.name: OsAlarmAction
children.description: This container defines which type of notification is used when the alarm expires.

children.name: OsAlarmActivateTask
children.description: This container specifies the parameters to activate a task.

children.name: OsAlarmActivateTaskRef
children.description: Reference to the task that will be activated by that alarm action

children.name: OsAlarmCallback
children.description: This container specifies the parameters to call a callback OS alarm action.

children.name: OsAlarmCallbackName
children.description: Name of the function that is called when this alarm callback is triggered.

children.name: OsAlarmIncrementCounter
children.description: This container specifies the parameters to increment a counter.

children.name: OsAlarmIncrementCounterRef
children.description: Reference to the counter that will be incremented by that alarm action

children.name: OsAlarmSetEvent
children.description: This container specifies the parameters to set an event

children.name: OsAlarmSetEventRef
children.description: Reference to the event that will be set by that alarm action

children.name: OsAlarmSetEventTaskRef
children.description: Reference to the task that will be activated by that event

children.name: OsAlarmAutostart
children.description: If present this container defines if an alarm is started automatically at system start-up depending on the application mode.

children.name: OsAlarmAlarmTime
children.description: The relative or absolute tick value when the alarm expires for the first time. Note that for an alarm which is RELATIVE the value must be at bigger than 0.

children.name: OsAlarmAutostartType
children.description: This specifies the type of autostart for the alarm..

children.name: OsAlarmCycleTime
children.description: Cycle time of a cyclic alarm in ticks. If the value is 0 than the alarm is not cyclic.

children.name: OsAlarmAppModeRef
children.description: Reference to the application modes for which the AUTOSTART shall be performed

children.name: OsAppMode
children.description: OsAppMode is the object used to define OSEK OS properties for an OSEK OS application mode.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: No standard attributes are defined for AppMode. In a CPU, at least one AppMode object has to be defined. [source: OSEK OIL Spec. 2.5] An OsAppMode called OSDEFAULTAPPMODE must always be there for OSEK compatibility.

children.name: OsApplication
children.description: An AUTOSAR OS must be capable of supporting a collection of OS objects (tasks, interrupts, alarms, hooks etc.) that form a cohesive functional unit. This collection of objects is termed an OS-Application.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: All objects which belong to the same OS-Application have access to each other. Access means to allow to use these objects within API services. Access by other applications can be granted separately.

children.name: OsTrusted
children.description: Parameter to specify if an OS-Application is trusted or not.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: OS-Application is trusted false: OS-Application is not trusted (default)

children.name: OsTrustedApplicationDelayTimingViolationCall
children.description: Parameter to specify if a timing violation which occurs within an trusted OS-Application is raised immediately of if it is delayed until the current task returns to the calling OS-Application (return of CallTrustedFunction)

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: violation / call to ProtectionHook() is delayed false: timing violation cause an immediate call to the ProtectionHook().

children.name: OsTrustedApplicationWithProtection
children.description: Parameter to specify if a trusted OS-Application is executed with memory protection or not.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: OS-Application runs within a protected environment. This means that write access is limited. false: OS-Application has full write access (default)

children.name: OsAppAlarmRef
children.description: Specifies the OsAlarms that belong to the OsApplication.

children.name: OsAppCounterRef
children.description: References the OsCounters that belong to the OsApplication.

children.name: OsAppEcucPartitionRef
children.description: Denotes which "EcucPartition" is implemented by this "OSApplication".

children.name: OsAppIsrRef
children.description: references which OsIsrs belong to the OsApplication

children.name: OsAppScheduleTableRef
children.description: References the OsScheduleTables that belong to the OsApplication.

children.name: OsAppTaskRef
children.description: references which OsTasks belong to the OsApplication

children.name: OsRestartTask
children.description: Optionally one task of an OS-Application may be defined as Restart Task.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: Multiplicity = 1: Restart Task is activated by the Operating System if the protection hook requests it. Multiplicity = 0: No task is automatically started after a protection error happened.

children.name: OsApplicationCoreRef
children.description: Reference to the Core Definition in the Ecuc Module where the CoreId is defined. This reference is used to describe to which Core the OsApplication is bound.

children.name: OsApplicationHooks
children.description: Container to structure the OS-Application-specific hooks

children.name: OsAppErrorHook
children.description: Select the OS-Application error hook.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsAppShutdownHook
children.description: Select the OS-Application specific shutdown hook for the OS-Application.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsAppStartupHook
children.description: Select the OS-Application specific startup hook for the OS-Application.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsApplicationTrustedFunction
children.description: Container to structure the configuration parameters of trusted functions

children.name: OsTrustedFunctionName
children.description: Trusted function (as part of a trusted OS-Application) available to other OS-Applications. This also supersedes the OSEK OIL attribute TRUSTED in APPLICATION because the optionality of this parameter is describing that already.

children.name: OsCounter
children.description: Configuration information for the counters that belong to the OsApplication.

children.name: OsCounterMaxAllowedValue
children.description: Maximum possible allowed value of the system counter in ticks.

children.name: OsCounterMinCycle
children.description: The MINCYCLE attribute specifies the minimum allowed number of counter ticks for a cyclic alarm linked to the counter.

children.name: OsCounterTicksPerBase
children.description: The TICKSPERBASE attribute specifies the number of ticks required to reach a counterspecific unit. The interpretation is implementation-specific.

children.name: OsCounterType
children.description: This parameter contains the natural type or unit of the counter.

children.name: OsSecondsPerTick
children.description: Time of one counter tick in seconds.

children.name: OsCounterAccessingApplication
children.description: Reference to applications which have an access to this object.

children.name: OsDriver
children.description: This Container contains the information who will drive the counter.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: This configuration is only valid if the counter has OsCounterType set to HARDWARE. If the container does not exist (multiplicity=0) the timer is managed by the OS internally (OSINTERNAL). If the container exists the OS can use the GPT interface to manage the timer. The user have to supply the GPT channel. If the counter is driven by some other (external to the OS) source (like a TPU for example) this must be described as a vendor specific extension.

children.name: OsGptChannelRef
children.description: Reference to the GPT channel.

children.name: OsTimeConstant
children.description: Allows the user to define constants which can be e.g. used to compare time values with timer tick values.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: A time value will be converted to a timer tick value during generation and can later on accessed via the OsConstName. The conversation is done by rounding time values to the nearest fitting tick value.

children.name: OsTimeValue
children.description: This parameter contains the value of the constant in seconds.

children.name: OsEvent
children.description: Representation of OS events in the configuration context. Adopted from the OSEK OIL specification.

children.name: OsEventMask
children.description: If event mask would be set to AUTO in OIL, this parameter should be omitted here.

children.name: OsIoc
children.description: Configuration of the IOC (Inter OS Application Communicator).

children.name: OsIocCommunication
children.description: Representation of a 1:1 or N:1 or N:M (unqueued only) communication between software parts located in different OS-Applications that are bound to the same or to different cores.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: The name shall begin with the name of the sending software service and be followed by a unique identifier delivered by the sending software service. In the case of RTE as user attention shall be paid on the fact that uniqueness for identifier names has to be reached over ports, data elements, object instances and maybe additional identification properties (E.g. Case 1:N mapping to 1:1). Example: - <NameSpace>_UniqueID

children.name: OsIocBufferLength
children.description: This attribute defines the size of the IOC internal queue to be allocated for a queued communication.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: This configuration information shall allow the optimization of the needed memory for communications requiring buffers within the RTE and within the IOC.

children.name: OsIocDataProperties
children.description: Data properties of the data to be transferred on the IOC communication channel.

children.name: OsIocDataPropertyIndex
children.description: This parameter is used to define in which order the data is send, e.g. whether IocSendGroup(A,B) or IocSendGroup(B,A) shall be used.

children.name: OsIocInitValue
children.description: Initial Value for the data to be transferred on the IOC communication channel.

children.name: OsIocDataTypeRef
children.description: This is the type of the data to be transferred on the IOC communication channel. This attribute is necessary to generate the parameter type of the Ioc functions. Additionally this information should be used to compute the data size for necessary data copy operations within the Ioc module.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: If more than one attribute is defined, the IOC generator should generate an IocXxxGroup function (Xxx= CHOICE [Send, Receive, Write, Read]). N:1 or N:M communication (Multiplicity of OsIocSenderProperties > 1) is only allowed for multiplicity of OsIocDataTypeRef = 1

children.name: OsIocReceiverProperties
children.description: Representation of receiver properties for one communication. For each OsIocCommunication one (1:1) or many receivers (N:M) have to be defined. This container should be instantiated within an OsIocCommunication.

children.name: OsIocFunctionImplementationKind
children.description: This parameter is used to select whether this communication is implemented as a macro or as a function.

metadata.LITERALS: DO_NOT_CARE AUTOSAR_ECUC FUNCTION AUTOSAR_ECUC MACRO AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsIocReceiverPullCB
children.description: This attribute defines the name of a callback function that the IOC shall call on the receiving core for each data reception.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: In case of non existence of this attribute no ReceiverPullCB notification shall be applied by the IOC. The name of the function shall begin with the name of the receiving module, followed with a callback name and followed by the IocId. Example: void RTE_ReceiverPullCB_RTE25 (void). If this attribute does not exist, it means that no ReceiverPullCB shall be called (No notification from IOC is required). If this attribute exists the IOC shall call the callback function on the receiving core.

children.name: OsIocReceivingOsApplicationRef
children.description: This attribute is a reference to the receiving OsApplication instance defined in the configuration file of the OS.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: This information allows for the generator to get additional information necessary for the code generation like: * The protection properties of the communicating OsApplications to find out which protections have to be crossed * The core identifiers to find out if an intra or an inter core communication has to be realized * Interrupt details in case of cross core notification to realize over IRQs

children.name: OsIocSenderProperties
children.description: Representation of sender properties for one communication. For each OsIocCommunication one (1:1) or many senders (N:1 or N:M) have to be defined. Multiplicity > 1 (N:1 or N:M communication) is only allowed for Multiplicity of OsIocDataTypeRef = 1.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: This container should be instantiated within an OsIocCommunication.

children.name: OsIocFunctionImplementationKind
children.description: This parameter is used to select whether this communication is implemented as a macro or as a function.

metadata.LITERALS: DO_NOT_CARE AUTOSAR_ECUC FUNCTION AUTOSAR_ECUC MACRO AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsIocSenderId
children.description: Representation of a sender in a N:1 or N:M communication to distinguish between senders.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: This parameter does not exist in 1:1 communication.

children.name: OsIocSendingOsApplicationRef
children.description: This attribute is a reference to the sending OS-Application instance defined in the configuration file of the OS.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: This information shall allows the generator to get additional information necessary for the code generation like: * The protection properties of the communicating OS-Applications to find out which protection boundaries have to be crossed. * The core identifiers to find out if an intra or an inter core communication has to be realized * Interrupt details in case of cross core notification to realize over IRQs

children.name: OsIsr
children.description: The OsIsr container represents an OSEK interrupt service routine.

children.name: OsIsrCategory
children.description: This attribute specifies the category of this ISR.

children.name: OsIsrResourceRef
children.description: This reference defines the resources accessed by this ISR.

children.name: OsIsrTimingProtection
children.description: This container contains all parameters which are related to timing protection

metadata.INTRODUCTION: If the container exists, the timing protection is used for this interrupt. If the container does not exist, the interrupt is not supervised regarding timing violations.

children.name: OsIsrAllInterruptLockBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum time for which the ISR is allowed to lock all interrupts (via SuspendAllInterrupts() or DisableAllInterrupts()) (in seconds).

children.name: OsIsrExecutionBudget
children.description: The parameter contains the maximum allowed execution time of the interrupt (in seconds).

children.name: OsIsrOsInterruptLockBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum time for which the ISR is allowed to lock all Category 2 interrupts (via SuspendOSInterrupts()) (in seconds).

children.name: OsIsrTimeFrame
children.description: This parameter contains the minimum inter-arrival time between successive interrupts (in seconds).

children.name: OsIsrResourceLock
children.description: This container contains a list of times the interrupt uses resources.

children.name: OsIsrResourceLockBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum time the interrupt is allowed to hold the given resource (in seconds).

children.name: OsIsrResourceLockResourceRef
children.description: Reference to the resource the locking time is depending on

children.name: OsOS
children.description: OS is the object used to define OSEK OS properties for an OSEK application.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: Per CPU exactly one OS object has to be defined.

children.name: OsNumberOfCores
children.description: Maximum number of cores that are controlled by the OS.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: The OS uses the value internally. It depends on the ECU HW.

children.name: OsScalabilityClass
children.description: A scalability class for each System Object "OS" has to be selected. In order to customize the operating system to the needs of the user and to take full advantage of the processor features the operating system can be scaled according to the scalability classes.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: If the scalability class is omitted this translates to the OIL AUTO mechanism.
metadata.LITERALS: SC1 AUTOSAR_ECUC SC2 AUTOSAR_ECUC SC3 AUTOSAR_ECUC SC4 AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsStackMonitoring
children.description: Select stack monitoring of Tasks/Category 2 ISRs

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Stacks are monitored false: Stacks are not monitored

children.name: OsStatus
children.description: The Status attribute specifies whether a system with standard or extended status has to be used. Automatic assignment is not supported for this attribute.

children.name: OsUseGetServiceId
children.description: As defined by OSEK

children.name: OsUseParameterAccess
children.description: As defined by OSEK

children.name: OsUseResScheduler
children.description: The OsUseResScheduler attribute defines whether the resource RES_SCHEDULER is used within the application.

children.name: OsHooks
children.description: Container to structure all hooks belonging to the OS

children.name: OsErrorHook
children.description: Error hook as defined by OSEK

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsPostTaskHook
children.description: Post-task hook as defined by OSEK

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsPreTaskHook
children.description: Pre-task hook as defined by OSEK

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsProtectionHook
children.description: Switch to enable/disable the call to the (user supplied) protection hook.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Protection hook is called on protection error false: Protection hook is not called

children.name: OsShutdownHook
children.description: Shutdown hook as defined by OSEK

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsStartupHook
children.description: Startup hook as defined by OSEK

metadata.INTRODUCTION: true: Hook is called false: Hook is not called

children.name: OsResource
children.description: An OsResource object is used to co-ordinate the concurrent access by tasks and ISRs to a shared resource, e.g. the scheduler, any program sequence, memory or any hardware area.

children.name: OsResourceProperty
children.description: This specifies the type of the resource.

metadata.LITERALS: INTERNAL AUTOSAR_ECUC LINKED AUTOSAR_ECUC STANDARD AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsResourceAccessingApplication
children.description: Reference to applications which have an access to this object.

children.name: OsResourceLinkedResourceRef
children.description: The link to the resource. Must be valid if OsResourceProperty is LINKED. If OsResourceProperty is not LINKED the value is ignored.

children.name: OsScheduleTable
children.description: An OsScheduleTable addresses the synchronization issue by providing an encapsulation of a statically defined set of alarms that cannot be modified at runtime.

children.name: OsScheduleTableDuration
children.description: This parameter defines the modulus of the schedule table (in ticks).

children.name: OsScheduleTableRepeating
children.description: true: first expiry point on the schedule table shall be processed at final expiry point delay ticks after the final expiry point is processed.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: false: the schedule table processing stops when the final expiry point is processed.

children.name: OsSchTblAccessingApplication
children.description: Reference to applications which have an access to this object.

children.name: OsScheduleTableCounterRef
children.description: This parameter contains a reference to the counter which drives the schedule table.

children.name: OsScheduleTableAutostart
children.description: This container specifies if and how the schedule table is started on startup of the Operating System. The options to start a schedule table correspond to the API calls to start schedule tables during runtime.

children.name: OsScheduleTableAutostartType
children.description: This specifies the type of the autostart for the schedule table.

metadata.LITERALS: ABSOLUTE AUTOSAR_ECUC RELATIVE AUTOSAR_ECUC SYNCHRON AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsScheduleTableStartValue
children.description: Absolute autostart tick value when the schedule table starts. Only used if the OsScheduleTableAutostartType is ABSOLUTE.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: Relative offset in ticks when the schedule table starts. Only used if the OsScheduleTableAutostartType is RELATIVE.

children.name: OsScheduleTableAppModeRef
children.description: Reference in which application modes the schedule table should be started during startup

children.name: OsScheduleTableExpiryPoint
children.description: The point on a Schedule Table at which the OS activates tasks and/or sets events

children.name: OsScheduleTblExpPointOffset
children.description: The offset from zero (in ticks) at which the expiry point is to be processed.

children.name: OsScheduleTableEventSetting
children.description: Event that is triggered by that schedule table.

children.name: OsScheduleTableSetEventRef
children.description: Reference to event that will be set by action

children.name: OsScheduleTableTaskActivation
children.description: Task that is triggered by that schedule table.

children.name: OsScheduleTableActivateTaskRef
children.description: Reference to task that will be activated by action

children.name: OsScheduleTblAdjustableExpPoint
children.description: Adjustable expiry point

children.name: OsScheduleTableMaxLengthen
children.description: The maximum positive adjustment that can be made to the expiry point offset (in ticks).

children.name: OsScheduleTableMaxShorten
children.description: The maximum negative adjustment that can be made to the expiry point offset (in ticks).

children.name: OsScheduleTableSync
children.description: This container specifies the synchronization parameters of the schedule table.

children.name: OsScheduleTblExplicitPrecision
children.description: This configuration is only valid if the explicit synchronization is used.

children.name: OsScheduleTblSyncStrategy
children.description: AUTOSAR OS provides support for synchronization in two ways: explicit and implicit.

metadata.LITERALS: EXPLICIT AUTOSAR_ECUC IMPLICIT AUTOSAR_ECUC NONE AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsSpinlock
children.description: An OsSpinlock object is used to co-ordinate concurrent access by TASKs/ISR2s on different cores to a shared resource.

children.name: OsSpinlockLockMethod
children.description: Lock method which is used when a spinlock is taken. Note that it is possible that a user (e.g. a Task) might hold more than one spinlock. In this case the last lock taken is forced to use at least a lock methode which locks as strong as the current one.

metadata.LITERALS: LOCK_ALL_INTERRUPTS AUTOSAR_ECUC LOCK_CAT2_INTERRUPTS AUTOSAR_ECUC LOCK_NOTHING AUTOSAR_ECUC LOCK_WITH_RES_SCHEDULER AUTOSAR_ECUC

children.name: OsSpinlockAccessingApplication
children.description: Reference to OsApplications that have an access to this object.

children.name: OsSpinlockSuccessor
children.description: Reference to OsApplications that have an access to this object.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: To check whether a spinlock can be occupied (in a nested way) without any danger of deadlock, a linked list of spinlocks can be defined. A spinlock can only be occupied in the order of the linked list. It is allowed to skip a spinlock. If no linked list is specified, spinlocks cannot be nested.

children.name: OsTask
children.description: This container represents an OSEK task.

children.name: OsTaskActivation
children.description: This attribute defines the maximum number of queued activation requests for the task. A value equal to "1" means that at any time only a single activation is permitted for this task. Note that the value must be a natural number starting at 1.

children.name: OsTaskPriority
children.description: The priority of a task is defined by the value of this attribute. This value has to be understood as a relative value, i.e. the values show only the relative ordering of the tasks.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: OSEK OS defines the lowest priority as zero (0); larger values correspond to higher priorities.

children.name: OsTaskSchedule
children.description: The OsTaskSchedule attribute defines the preemptability of the task.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: If this attribute is set to NON, no internal resources may be assigned to this task.

children.name: OsTaskAccessingApplication
children.description: Reference to applications which have an access to this object.

children.name: OsTaskEventRef
children.description: This reference defines the list of events the extended task may react on.

children.name: OsTaskResourceRef
children.description: This reference defines a list of resources accessed by this task.

children.name: OsTaskAutostart
children.description: This container determines whether the task is activated during the system start-up procedure or not for some specific application modes.

metadata.INTRODUCTION: If the task shall be activated during the system start-up, this container is present and holds the references to the application modes in which the task is auto-started.

children.name: OsTaskAppModeRef
children.description: Reference to application modes in which that task is activated on startup of the OS

children.name: OsTaskTimingProtection
children.description: This container contains all parameters regarding timing protection of the task.

children.name: OsTaskAllInterruptLockBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum time for which the task is allowed to lock all interrupts (via SuspendAllInterrupts() or DisableAllInterrupts()) (in seconds).

children.name: OsTaskExecutionBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum allowed execution time of the task (in seconds).

children.name: OsTaskOsInterruptLockBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum time for which the task is allowed to lock all Category 2 interrupts (via SuspendOSInterrupts()) (in seconds).

children.name: OsTaskTimeFrame
children.description: The minimum inter-arrival time between activations and/or releases of a task (in seconds).

children.name: OsTaskResourceLock
children.description: This container contains the worst case time between getting and releasing a given resource (in seconds).

children.name: OsTaskResourceLockBudget
children.description: This parameter contains the maximum time the task is allowed to lock the resource (in seconds)

children.name: OsTaskResourceLockResourceRef
children.description: Reference to the resource used by the task
